genes.name: WAGR syndrome
genes.role: About 33% develop a childhood renal embryonal tumor; with aniridia, genital anomalies and intellectual disability

genes.name: Denys-Drash syndrome
genes.role: About 90% develop a childhood renal embryonal tumor; with gonadal dysgenesis and renal failure from diffuse mesangial sclerosis

genes.name: Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome
genes.role: Organomegaly, macroglossia, hemihypertrophy, omphalocele and enlarged adrenals, with raised childhood renal tumor risk

genes.name: Wilms tumor with focal anaplasia
genes.role: Seen in the undifferentiated, pleomorphic areas; these children tend to resist chemotherapy
avoid: Invasive urothelial carcinoma of the renal pelvis

genes.name: Noninvasive papillary urothelial carcinoma
genes.gene: FGFR3 amplification with activating RAS and PI3-kinase mutations
genes.role: Gain in growth factor receptor signaling; the commonest pathway: tumors recur often but invade muscle in only about 20%

genes.name: Urothelial carcinoma in situ (flat pathway)
genes.role: High-grade, multifocal, confined to the epithelium at first, yet the precursor of most muscle-invasive bladder cancer

genes.name: Superficial urothelial carcinoma of the renal pelvis
genes.role: Seen in noninvasive tumors of the pelvicalyceal lining; smoking is the big risk factor

genes.name: Invasive urothelial carcinoma of the renal pelvis
genes.role: Marks the tumors that have grown beyond the lining of the upper collecting system
